verses.english: “Mendicants, suppose there was a sharp-pointed spear.
And a man came along and thought,

verses.pali: ‘ahaṁ imaṁ sattiṁ tiṇhaphalaṁ pāṇinā vā muṭṭhinā vā paṭileṇissāmi paṭikoṭṭissāmi paṭivaṭṭessāmī’ti.
verses.english: ‘With my hand or fist I’ll fold this sharp spear over, crumple it, and bend it back!’

verses.pali: bhabbo nu kho so puriso amuṁ sattiṁ tiṇhaphalaṁ pāṇinā vā muṭṭhinā vā paṭileṇetuṁ paṭikoṭṭetuṁ paṭivaṭṭetun”ti?
verses.english: Is that man capable of doing so?”

verses.pali: “Asu hi, bhante, satti tiṇhaphalā na sukarā pāṇinā vā muṭṭhinā vā paṭileṇetuṁ paṭikoṭṭetuṁ paṭivaṭṭetuṁ.
verses.english: Because it’s not easy to fold that sharp spear over, crumple it, and bend it back with the hand or fist.

verses.pali: Yāvadeva ca pana so puriso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā”ti.
verses.english: That man will eventually get weary and frustrated.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhuno mettācetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, tassa ce amanusso cittaṁ khipitabbaṁ maññeyya;
verses.english: “In the same way, suppose a mendicant has developed the heart’s release by love, has cultivated it, made it a vehicle and a basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it. Should any non-human think to overthrow their mind,

verses.pali: atha kho sveva amanusso kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assa.
verses.english: they’ll eventually get weary and frustrated.
So you should train like this:

verses.pali: ‘mettā no cetovimutti bhāvitā bhavissati bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā’ti.
verses.english: ‘We will develop the heart’s release by love. We’ll cultivate it, make it our vehicle and our basis, keep it up, consolidate it, and properly implement it.’
